subject: Plan composition & upgrade/downgrade options for PixelHealth rollout
messages:
From: Emma Li <emma@pixelhealth.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
Cc: PixelHealth Procurement <procurement@pixelhealth.com>
Date: Fri, 10 Apr 2027 09:05:00 -0700
Subject: Plan options and bundling question for PixelHealth rollout

Hi Soojin,

Thanks again for the demo last week — the latency numbers look promising. We're starting to map our rollout and need guidance on the right plan mix. A quick summary of our needs:
- Multi-region inference (US primary, EU DR)
- ~6M tokens/month initially, predictable spikes around product launches
- Long-term need for dedicated capacity and tighter SLAs, but want to start with low friction onboarding

Questions:
1) If we start on Hosted and later move to Dedicated, how smooth is the upgrade? Is there a migration window or downtime?
2) What does a downgrade look like if we end up below committed usage after 6 months?
3) Can you bundle Redwood Optimize + Console with Dedicated and do you offer onboarding credits or first-year discounts for mid-market customers?

Appreciate a short summary and a couple of concrete paths (start Hosted -> Dedicated, or go Dedicated from day 1) so we can pick and present to procurement.

—Emma
Emma Li
Head of AI Product, PixelHealth
emma@pixelhealth.com
From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
To: Emma Li <emma@pixelhealth.com>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 10 Apr 2027 11:20:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Plan options and bundling question for PixelHealth rollout

Emma — great questions. Short answer: both paths are viable; I'll outline tradeoffs and a recommended commercial frame below. I've attached a one-page pricing summary and a migration timetable.

Path A — Start Hosted (recommended for first 1–3 months):
- Pros: fastest time-to-value, no infra commit, minimal legal review
- Cons: slightly higher per-token cost, limited SLA compared to Dedicated
- Migration to Dedicated: supported with automated model/version migration and a scheduled cutover window. Typical migration takes 24–72 hours of planned work with no model code changes required; we provide a runbook and can run a canary for traffic split.

Path B — Dedicated from day 1 (recommended if you need strict latency/SLA and expect steady load):
- Pros: predictable unit costs, reserved GPU capacity, SLA-backed latency and uptime
- Cons: procurement lead time, 12-month commit typically required for favorable pricing

Downgrade policy (if you commit and later need to reduce):
- We offer a 60-day notice window. For reductions in committed capacity within the first 6 months we apply a stepdown schedule (prorated credits applied; see attached sheet for examples). We can discuss a limited one-time stepdown exception for orgs with legitimate market shifts.

Bundling & discounts:
- We can bundle Redwood Optimize + Console with Dedicated under a single SKU.
- Typical mid-market packaging: Dedicated (reserved GPU pool) + Optimize + 12-month support retention = ~10% list discount off Hosted-equivalent spend, or an onboarding credit instead.

Suggested commercial anchor for PixelHealth (proposal):
- 12-month Dedicated commit sized to expected steady-state (proposal: 2x standard GPU nodes; estimate in attached spreadsheet)
- Bundled Optimize + Console included
- Commercial offer: 10% first-year discount + $7,000 onboarding credit OR 12% if you sign a 24-month commit

Next steps: I can set up a 30-minute sync with procurement and our solutions engineer to walk the migration timetable and redline SOW. Are you available Mon 4/13 or Tue 4/14?

Attachments: pixelhealth_pricing_summary.xlsx, pixelhealth_migration_timetable.pdf

Best,
Soojin Lee
Senior Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference
soojin_lee@redwood.com
From: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 10 Apr 2027 13:00:00 -07:00
Subject: Fwd: Plan options and bundling question for PixelHealth rollout

Looping you both in — quick internal note on the commercial posture for PixelHealth:

- Customer signals they prefer low-friction start but will need Dedicated within 3–6 months.
- Recommend we lead with 12-month Dedicated anchor, but offer Hosted pilot (30–60 days) that rolls into the commit. That reduces procurement friction and preserves the economic commitment.
- Discounting: I'm comfortable with 10% + $7k onboarding credit for 12-month commit. If they insist on a shorter commit, push to 10% but reduce credit to $4k.
- Keep Optimize & Console bundled; they're strategic win conditions and reduce churn risk.

Action: Soojin, if you agree I propose to present the 10%/7k option and the Hosted-pilot -> Dedicated migration runbook in the call.

—Lauren
VP, Mid-Market Sales, Redwood Inference
lauren_bishop@redwood.com
From: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
To: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 10 Apr 2027 15:10:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Plan options and bundling question for PixelHealth rollout

Thanks — I like the pilot -> commit approach. A couple of guardrails from GTM:
- Offer: 10% first-year discount + $7k onboarding credit on a 12-month Dedicated commit (no change to list if they choose 24-month; we can bump to 12%).
- Make the pilot explicit: 45-day Hosted pilot with a signed Letter of Intent to convert to Dedicated if metrics met (latency, cost per token, traffic thresholds). The LOI should include the conversion timeline so procurement has visibility.
- For stepdowns: cap stepdown exceptions to one time in the first contract year, with pro-rated credit applied.

I'll approve the 10%/7k as long as legal includes the LOI -> contract conversion language.

-Aditya
Head of Sales, Redwood Inference
aditya_rao@redwood.com
From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
To: Emma Li <emma@pixelhealth.com>
Cc: PixelHealth Procurement <procurement@pixelhealth.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 11 Apr 2027 08:30:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Plan options and bundling question for PixelHealth rollout

Emma — thanks for the quick context. Based on our internal alignment, here's a concise commercial proposal you can take to procurement:

Offer summary (anchor):
- 12-month Dedicated commit (sized to expected steady-state; details in attachment)
- Bundled: Redwood Optimize + Redwood Console included
- Commercial terms: 10% first-year discount off list, plus a $7,000 onboarding credit applied against first invoices
- Pilot option: 45-day Hosted pilot available. If pilot metrics are met and you sign LOI to convert, we migrate to Dedicated on an agreed cutover window (24–72 hours; runbook provided).
- Downgrade stepdown: one-time exception allowed during year 1 with pro-rated credit; thereafter standard stepdown schedule applies.

Attachments: pixelhealth_pricing_summary.xlsx, sow_pixelhealth_draft.docx, pixelhealth_migration_timetable.pdf

If that framing works, I'll route the SOW to legal and send a DocuSign for the LOI so procurement has something to execute quickly. Can we aim to have LOI signed the week of 4/19?

Best,
Soojin Lee
Senior Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference
